places.title: Erasmusbrug (Erasmus Bridge)
places.why: An 800-metre cable-stayed bridge whose bent white pylon, nicknamed the Swan, ties the old centre to the towers of Kop van Zuid. Walk across it, or watch it from the Maas quays at dusk.

places.title: Cube Houses, Witte Huis and the Oude Haven
places.architect: Piet Blom (Cube Houses); Willem Molenbroek (Witte Huis)
places.why: Piet Blom's yellow cubes, tilted 45 degrees on concrete stalks, form a forest of houses over a road bridge beside the city's oldest harbour. Across the water stands the Witte Huis of 1898, an early Art Nouveau high-rise that survived the 1940 bombing.

photos.file: Cube Houses Rotterdam Modern Architecture Netherlands 2026.jpg
photos.author: Tolga Bakı

places.title: Markthal
places.why: A horseshoe of 228 flats arching over a covered food market, its glass end walls hung on cable nets. Inside, a giant printed artwork of fruit, fish and flowers covers the whole vault.

places.title: Van Nelle Factory (Van Nellefabriek)
places.architect: Brinkman & Van der Vlugt (with Mart Stam)
places.why: A tobacco, coffee and tea factory wrapped in glass curtain walls on mushroom columns, with diagonal conveyor bridges crossing to the canal-side warehouses. A UNESCO World Heritage site and the purest work of Dutch functionalism, now used as offices and event halls.

places.title: Euromast and Het Park
places.architect: Hugh Maaskant (Euromast); J.D. and L.P. Zocher (Het Park)
places.why: Maaskant's concrete observation tower, raised to 185 m in 1970, gives the classic view over the river and the port. At its foot lies Het Park, a 19th-century landscape park by the Zochers with old trees and ponds, and the walled historic garden of Schoonoord.

photos.file: Rotterdam Northern portal of Maastunnel and Euromast seen from 3e Katendrechtsehoofd.jpg
photos.author: Ymblanter

photos.file: Het Park @ Observation deck @ Euromast @ Rotterdam (30604512105).jpg
photos.author: Guilhem Vellut from Annecy, France

photos.file: Het Park, Rotterdam in the morning 2024-12-03.jpg
photos.author: Andy Li

places.title: Historic Delfshaven
places.why: The old harbour of Delft escaped the 1940 bombing: a canal lined with gabled warehouses, a rebuilt grain mill, the church where the Pilgrim Fathers worshipped before sailing for America in 1620, and small quays full of cafés.

photos.file: Zicht op de Voorhaven en Piet Heynsbrug vanaf de Mouterbrug (2020).jpg
photos.author: MatteoNL97

photos.file: Traditionele huizen aan de Voorhaven met de Piet Heynsbrug (2021).jpg
photos.author: MatteoNL97

photos.file: Rotterdam-Delfshaven, windkorenmolen de Distilleerketel RM32880 foto3 2015-08-02 10.44.jpg
photos.author: Michielverbeek

places.title: Wilhelminapier and Kop van Zuid
places.architect: Foster + Partners, Renzo Piano, Mecanoo, Álvaro Siza and others
places.why: The pier from which the Holland America Line carried emigrants to New York is now Rotterdam's skyline of towers by Foster, Piano, Mecanoo and Siza. The line's Art Nouveau head office survives at the tip as Hotel New York, and the Santos warehouse now houses the Nederlands Fotomuseum.

photos.file: Rotterdam - 3072 - 2024.01.07 - Hôtel New York © Anthony Levrot.jpg
photos.author: Anthony Levrot

places.title: Kinderdijk windmills
places.why: Nineteen drainage mills of brick and thatch line two polder canals, the largest group of old windmills in the Netherlands and a lesson in how the country was kept dry. Reached from Rotterdam by waterbus.

places.title: Coolsingel and City Hall
places.architect: Henri Evers (City Hall); G.C. Bremer (Post Office); ODA (Post tower)
places.why: The city's main boulevard, redesigned with wide tree-lined promenades. City Hall and the main post office are among the few pre-war buildings that survived the bombing; a new arched tower by ODA now rises behind the post office.

places.title: Grote of Sint-Laurenskerk
places.why: The only medieval building left in the centre: a Late Gothic church gutted in 1940 and restored after the war, its stone tower a fixed point among the post-war blocks.

photos.author: FaceMePLS from The Hague, The Netherlands

places.title: Rotterdam Centraal
places.architect: Team CS (Benthem Crouwel, MVSA Architects, West 8)
places.why: The station's steel-clad hall points like a blade over the station square, with a warm timber ceiling beneath. Behind it, a long glass roof partly covered in solar cells shelters the platforms.

photos.author: Nanda Sluijsmans from Den Haag, Nederland

places.title: Museumpark
places.why: A park laid out by OMA and landscape architect Yves Brunier as a sequence of distinct zones between the museums. It ties together the Kunsthal, the Depot, Het Nieuwe Instituut, the Chabot Museum and Sonneveld House.

places.title: Witte de Withstraat
places.why: A short 19th-century street between the Museumpark and the old harbours, lined with galleries, an art institute, small shops and restaurants; the liveliest street of the centre in the evening.

photos.author: FaceMePLS from The Hague, The Netherlands

photos.file: 2024 Witte de Withstraat, Rotterdam hoek Zwarte Paardenstraat gezien vanaf de Witte de Wiithstraat.jpg
photos.author: Marcel Douwe Dekker

places.title: De Rotterdam
places.why: Three stacked and shifted towers of offices, flats and a hotel make a vertical city 150 m high. Its massing changes with every step you take along the Erasmus Bridge.

photos.file: De Rotterdam @ Wilhelminapier @ Kop van Zuid @ Rotterdam (30447701252).jpg
photos.author: Guilhem Vellut from Annecy, France

places.title: Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen
places.why: A 40-metre bowl clad in mirror panels that reflects the park and the city, holding the museum’s whole collection in open storage. Birch trees grow on the roof terrace.

places.title: Kunsthal
places.why: Koolhaas's exhibition hall is a box cut through by a road and a public ramp, mixing cheap and noble materials: corrugated plastic, raw steel, tree-trunk columns.

places.title: Het Nieuwe Instituut
places.why: Home of the national architecture archive: a glass block over a pond, a long archive wing raised on columns along the street, and a curved exhibition hall.

places.title: Sonneveld House (Huis Sonneveld)
places.why: A white villa built for a director of the Van Nelle factory, with ribbon windows and steel balconies; its 1930s interior of tubular furniture and colour schemes is preserved as a house museum.

places.title: Chabot Museum
places.why: A white functionalist villa on the edge of the Museumpark, one of the few pre-war buildings in the area, now showing the work of the painter Henk Chabot.

places.title: Timmerhuis
places.why: A pixelated stack of glass modules rising in steps over the 1953 municipal building, with offices below, flats above and a public atrium linking it to the street.

photos.file: 2016 Het Timmerhuis op de hoek van de Haagseveer, gezien vanaf het Raam Raamplein.jpg
photos.author: Collectie: Collectie vrijwillige fotografen ; Vervaardiger: Sjef (S.) Middelweerd ; Auteursrechthouder: Gemeente Rotterdam (Stadsarchief) CC-0

places.title: Fenix
places.architect: Mei architects and planners; MAD Architects (Tornado)
places.why: The former San Francisco warehouse on the Rijnhaven, once the largest in the world, now holds a museum of migration crowned by the Tornado, a double spiral stair of steel and wood. Its western part was turned into lofts lifted above the old roof.

places.title: Book Mountain (Boekenberg)
places.why: A pyramid of bookshelves under a glass barn roof on the market square of Spijkenisse, climbed by stairs and terraces to a reading café at the top. On metro line D.

photos.file: Boekenberg de bekende bibliotheek in Spijkenisse.jpg
photos.author: Peter van der Sluijs

places.title: New Luxor Theatre
places.why: A red theatre at the foot of the Erasmus Bridge, whose foyer ramps spiral around the auditorium and open in a big window towards the Maas.

photos.file: 2015 Nieuwe Luxortheater en De Rotterdam gezien vanaf de Posthumalaan, Rotterdam.jpg
photos.author: Vervaardiger: Mark (M.) Roestenburg ; Auteursrechthouder: Gemeente Rotterdam (Stadsarchief) CC-0

places.title: Pauluskerk
places.why: Will Alsop's church and day centre for homeless people, a faceted copper-coloured volume pierced by triangular windows at the foot of a tower block.

places.title: Central Library (Centrale Bibliotheek)
places.why: A stepped building under a sloping glass roof, with bright yellow ventilation tubes running over its facades and a tall atrium inside.

photos.file: Centrale bibliotheek van Rotterdam en Blaaktoren - City of Rotterdam (21999005883).jpg
photos.author: Frans Berkelaar

places.title: St. Mary of the Angels Chapel
places.why: Mecanoo's small funeral chapel in the Roman Catholic cemetery of St. Laurentius: a curving deep-blue wall printed with text, under a gold-lined roof that seems to float on a band of glass.

places.title: Port Pavilion
places.why: A timber visitor pavilion on the Leuvehaven quay that introduces the port, with terraces over the oldest artificial harbour of the city.

places.title: Groothandelsgebouw
places.architect: Hugh Maaskant and Willem van Tijen
places.why: An enormous wholesale building around three courtyards, with an internal street that lorries could drive through. Built opposite the station, it became the symbol of the reconstruction.

places.title: Lijnbaan
places.why: Europe's first purpose-built pedestrian shopping street: two-storey shops under continuous canopies, with tall slabs of flats set back behind green courts.

photos.file: Rotterdam, de Lijnbaan in de rust van Excelsior-Feyenoord IMG 6497 2017-05-07 15.34.jpg
photos.author: Michielverbeek

places.title: De Kuip (Stadion Feijenoord)
places.why: Feyenoord's stadium, its stands hung from an exposed steel frame so that no columns block the view; a modernist landmark by the architects of the Van Nelle factory.

places.title: Diergaarde Blijdorp (Rotterdam Zoo)
places.why: The zoo was designed as a whole by Sybold van Ravesteyn around 1940; his curving pavilions, gates and the Rivièrahal survive among the newer enclosures.

photos.author: The original uploader was Sherpa at Dutch Wikipedia .

places.title: Erasmus MC
places.why: The new university hospital groups its wings along a long glass hall that works as an indoor street, beside the 1960s Dijkzigt tower.

places.title: Erasmus University Campus Woudestein
places.why: A post-war university campus reworked around a green central axis and water, with the modernist library given a new glass front.

photos.file: Rotterdam School of Management Erasmus University Campus spring.jpg
photos.author: RSM erasmus

places.title: Schiedam windmills
places.why: The tallest traditional windmills in the world, built to grind malt for Schiedam's gin distilleries, stand along the canals and old ramparts of the town.

photos.file: 033 Canals of Schiedam - Linquenda inland barge in Korte Haven, Schiedam, Netherlands - Gracht in Nederland.jpg
photos.author: Marek Ślusarczyk ( Tupungato ) Photo portfolio

places.title: Hofbogen and the Schieblock
places.why: A 1.9 km railway viaduct whose brick arches hold shops and cafés, with a raised park planned along its deck. It starts at the Schieblock, an office block saved from demolition with a rooftop farm and bar.
places.note: The yellow Luchtsingel footbridge that linked the Schieblock to the Hofbogen was taken down in 2024–2025; a new one is planned.

photos.file: Luchtpark Hofbogen - Agniesebuurt - Noord - Rotterdam - former railway platform - 2024 - pic1.jpg
photos.author: AgainErick

photos.file: DakAkker rooftopfarm tijdens Rotterdam Open Dakendagen, 2018.jpg
photos.author: tjabeljan

places.title: SS Rotterdam
places.why: The former flagship of the Holland America Line, moored for good as a hotel; its late-1950s interiors are among the best preserved of any ocean liner.

places.title: Portlantis
places.why: A ring-shaped visitor centre stacked on stilts at the edge of the Maasvlakte, with views over Europe’s largest port and the North Sea.

places.title: RiF010
places.why: A surfable wave built into the Steigersgracht, a city-centre canal next to the Markthal.

places.title: Floating Farm
places.why: A dairy farm floating in a former harbour basin: cows on the upper deck, milk processing below, and a pasture on the quay.

photos.file: 2024 Floating Farm in Rotterdam entry from shore to floating raft.jpg
photos.author: Marcel Douwe Dekker

photos.file: Floating Farm in the Maas river, Rotterdam, NL.jpg
photos.author: Paulswagerman

places.title: Floating Office Rotterdam
places.why: A floating timber office building with deep terraces and its own energy supply, moored in the Rijnhaven.

photos.file: The Netherlands, Rotterdam, Rijnhaven, Floating office designed by the Powerhouse Company, 2023.jpg
photos.author: Lark Ascending

places.title: Kiefhoek
places.why: Oud's workers' estate of tiny white terraced houses with primary-coloured doors and frames, a De Stijl palette applied to social housing. One house is open as a museum.

photos.file: Overzicht uiteinde straat eindigend in winkel in de wijk Kiefhoek van J.J.P. Oud - Rotterdam - 20536891 - RCE.jpg
photos.author: Paul van Galen

places.title: Justus van Effen Complex
places.why: A block of social housing with a raised deck at second-floor level running round the courtyard like an elevated street, a forerunner of the gallery flat.

places.title: Bergpolderflat
places.architect: Willem van Tijen, Brinkman & Van der Vlugt
places.why: The first gallery-access block of flats in the Netherlands: a slender steel frame with nine floors of identical flats reached by open galleries.

places.title: Little C
places.why: A compact new quarter of mixed blocks and towers around narrow streets and a raised green courtyard, mixing homes, workspaces and shops on the edge of the Coolhaven.

photos.author: Nanda Sluijsmans from Den Haag, Nederland
Nanda Sluijsmans from Den Haag, Nederland

places.title: SAWA
places.why: A 50-metre residential building built of cross-laminated timber, its planted terraces stepping down towards the Maas.

photos.file: 2025 Lloydstraat, Rotterdam met SAWA Rotterdam, het eerste houten woongebouw van ruim 50 meter hoog in Rotterdam.jpg
photos.author: Marcel Douwe Dekker

photos.file: 2025 Kartinistraat, Rotterdam met de plint van het SAWA houten woongebouw.jpg
photos.author: Marcel Douwe Dekker

places.title: De Zalmhaven
places.why: At 215 m the tallest building in the Netherlands, a slender residential tower over the old harbour quarter.

photos.file: Rotterdam De Zalmhaven I and Hoge Erasmus seen from Erasmus Bridge.jpg
photos.author: Ymblanter

photos.file: De Zalmhaven I, II and III - Rotterdam - View from the Veerhaven.jpg
photos.author: AgainErick

places.title: Didden Village
places.why: A blue rooftop village of small houses, trees and parapets added on top of an ordinary 19th-century house to give a family more room.

places.title: Katendrecht
places.why: A former harbour peninsula with a rough sailors' reputation, now a lively residential district around the Deliplein, with new housing at its heart and the Fenix warehouses on the Rijnhaven.

photos.file: 2025 Het 1e Katendrechtsehoofd, Rotterdam met De roeiers (2000) van Yair Aschkenasy.jpg
photos.author: Marcel Douwe Dekker

places.title: Kralingse Bos and Kralingse Plas
places.why: A large woodland park around a lake, laid out over four decades and opened in 1953, with beaches, rowing and two old snuff mills on the shore.

places.title: Trompenburg Gardens and Arboretum
places.why: A 19th-century estate garden turned arboretum, with rare trees, rhododendrons, rose gardens and glasshouses on the edge of Kralingen.

places.title: Vroesenpark
places.why: A landscape park laid out with the 1930s Blijdorp district, with wide lawns that fill up on summer days.

photos.file: 2024 Het Vroesenpaviljoen in het Vroesenpark in Rotterdam gezien vanuit het westen.jpg
photos.author: Marcel Douwe Dekker

places.title: Zuiderpark
places.why: One of the largest city parks in the Netherlands, made after the war for the southern districts, with woods, ponds and sports fields.

places.title: Dakpark
places.why: A park on top of a kilometre-long shopping building that also works as a dyke, overlooking the port basins of Vierhavens, with neighbourhood gardens and play areas.

photos.author: Vervaardiger: Sjef (S.) Middelweerd ; Auteursrechthouder: Gemeente Rotterdam (Stadsarchief) CC-0

places.title: Getijdenpark Keilehaven
places.why: A harbour quay broken open to let the tide in: mudflats, reeds and steps where the river rises and falls twice a day, built partly from recycled materials.

photos.author: AgainErick

photos.author: AgainErick

photos.author: AgainErick

places.title: Getijdenpark Eiland van Brienenoord
places.why: An island in the Nieuwe Maas under the motorway bridge, turned into a freshwater tidal park with creeks, willow woods and paths.

places.title: Buitenplaats De Tempel
places.why: An 18th-century country estate in the polder on the city edge, its house, ponds and garden restored as a public park.

photos.file: Overzicht voorgevel landhuis met gedeelte van park - Overschie - 20377864 - RCE.jpg
photos.author: Gerard Dukker

photos.file: Overzicht voorgevel met vijver met fontein, beelden en watervallen op de voorgrond - Overschie - 20358446 - RCE.jpg
photos.author: Gerard Dukker

places.title: Water Square Benthemplein
places.why: The first water square: three sunken basins used for sport and sitting that fill with rainwater during cloudbursts, fed by stainless steel gutters.

places.title: Afrikaanderpark
places.why: The central park of a multicultural district, redesigned around a looping path, lawns and play areas, with a market square on its edge.

places.title: Schouwburgplein
places.why: A raised square of steel, timber and rubber panels over a car park, lit by four tall red hydraulic lamps.

places.title: Rijnhaven
places.why: A former harbour basin between Katendrecht and the Wilhelminapier, being rewilded with a raised seabed, gardens on its banks and floating park islands.

photos.file: Drijvend Paviljoen, Rijnhaven Rotterdam - GraphyArchy - Wikipedia 00255.jpg
photos.author: GraphyArchy

places.title: Bergse Plassen
places.why: Two lakes in Hillegersberg framed by villas, rowing clubs and lakeside paths, with the Prinsenmolen windmill and park on the shore.

places.title: Wikado Playground
places.why: A playground built from five discarded wind-turbine blades, cut up and turned into towers, tunnels and slides.
